title: FedAvg with PyTorch state_dicts
learning_objectives: Average client state_dicts weighted by their sample counts
Handle integer buffers that must not be averaged
Run several federated rounds and watch the global model improve
entry_point: average_states(states, counts); federated_training(model, clients, rounds, epochs=1, lr=0.1, seed=0)
hints: Check `tensor.is_floating_point()` to decide between averaging and copying.
`sum(state[k] * (n / total) for state, n in zip(states, counts))` averages one tensor.
After each round, measure `nn.functional.mse_loss(model(X_all), y_all)` under `torch.no_grad()`.

failure_feedback.advice: Weight each client by n_i / total and copy integer tensors from the first state.
num_batches_tracked is an integer buffer: copy it instead of averaging.
Each round: update every client from the current model, average, load_state_dict.
Reject empty input, non-positive counts and mismatched keys.
